input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: The cap is mutual, indirect damages are mutually excluded (21.2), the Excluded Claims carve-outs in 21.3 cover confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and Customer's payment obligation is expressly not "damages" — all at or above the preferred position. The quantum, however, is illusory: "Fees" is defined (1.5) as the Implementation Fee, which is "the one-time implementation charge of USD 12,000 stated in the first Order Form" (1.8), and 21.1 further limits the basis to the first Order Form. The effective cap is therefore about USD 12,000 regardless of subscription spend — far below 12 months' fees and below even 6 months' charges, which is walk-away territory. Minimal fix: rebase 21.1 on all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding 12 months, with the USD 1,000,000 floor; no other part of Section 21 is touched.

proposal.summary: Fix illusory liability cap: base it on all amounts payable under the Agreement in the preceding 12 months, with a USD 1,000,000 floor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] As drafted the cap is tied to "Fees", which is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the mutual cap is illusory and sits far below our floor of 12 months' charges. We have changed the basis to the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000; indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations remain outside the cap under Section 21.3, which we are happy to leave as is.
